item.text:
**Verdict:** mixed, leaning no on a broad “better life chances” claim. Sharif’s 2024 government improved macro stability and formal safety-net delivery relative to a very weak inherited baseline, but the gains were modest, poverty still rose, and coercive treatment of protesters, minorities, refugees, and low-income residents undercut any strong claim of improved ordinary life chances.

**Accepted Claims**
- **Inherited baseline was severe** | **World Bank** | **2023-10-03** | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2023/10/02/fiscal-reforms-are-critical-for-economic-stability-sustainable-growth-in-pakistan) | Pakistan entered 2024 after contraction, flood damage, import controls, political uncertainty, high prices, and weak confidence. This matters because Sharif’s 2024 performance should be judged against a bad starting point. | `6B.10`
- **Macro stabilization improved, but not enough to lift poverty** | **World Bank** | **2024-10-10** | [URL](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank) | Growth recovered to 2.5 percent and conditions stabilized, but poverty still rose from 40.2 to 40.5 percent. That is the strongest single counterweight to any claim of broad life-chance gains. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.8`
- **IMF said the recovery was real but structurally incomplete** | **IMF** | **2024-09-27** | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/09/27/pr-24343-pakistan-imf-concludes-2024-aiv-consultation-pakistan-approves-37-mo-extended-arr) | Growth rebounded, inflation fell to single digits, and reserves rebuilt, but weak governance, low investment, and insufficient health and education spending remained major constraints. This supports “better than inherited, but still fragile.” | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.9`
- **The IMF-backed program explicitly aimed at broader-based resilience** | **IMF** | **2024-07-12** | [URL](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) | The program called for broader taxation, SOE reform, stronger competition, climate resilience, and expanded BISP/health/education spending. That is a genuine attempt to improve ordinary people’s prospects, even if results were incomplete. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.9`
- **BISP delivery became more transparent and scalable** | **APP** | **2024-03-18** | [URL](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-directs-full-digitalization-of-social-welfare-payments-under-bisp/) | Sharif ordered BISP payments onto digital “Social Protection Wallets” to reduce leakage, delays, and discretion. This is a concrete institutional improvement that could improve beneficiaries’ life chances if sustained. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- **Mass digital wallets for BISP beneficiaries launched** | **APP** | **2024-08-25** | [URL](https://www.app.com.pk/national/pm-shehbaz-launches-10-mln-bisp-digital-wallets-terms-landmark-step-towards-cashless-economy/) | The government launched 10 million BISP digital wallets, framing them as a step toward transparency, financial inclusion, and a cashless economy. This is one of the clearest positive delivery-side claims in 2024. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- **Education was elevated as a national emergency** | **Dawn** | **2024-04-10** | [URL](https://www.dawn.com/news/1826827) | Sharif announced an education emergency and said the state would expand Daanish Schools into underserved areas for poor children. That is a plausible long-horizon life-chance improvement, though still mainly a policy commitment. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- **Energy costs were eased through tariff renegotiation** | **Reuters / Dawn** | **2024-10-10** | [URL](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1864298) | The government renegotiated power contracts to cut tariffs and save about Rs60 billion a year. Lower power costs can improve household and business life chances, but this was still only a partial repair of a broader utility crisis. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.6`, `6B.8`
- **Low-income residents were forcibly evicted** | **Human Rights Watch** | **2024-05-28** | [URL](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/05/28/pakistan-abusive-evictions-target-urban-poor) | HRW reported forcible evictions of poor residents, shop owners, and vendors without adequate notice, compensation, or resettlement. This is direct evidence against improved life chances for marginalized urban households. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- **Afghan refugees lost safety and access to livelihood** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-04-04** | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/04/pakistan-government-must-halt-deportation-of-afghan-refugees/) | Amnesty said the repatriation plan lacked transparency and due process and threatened refugees’ safety, education, and livelihoods. That is negative evidence on whether ordinary vulnerable people had better prospects in 2024. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`
- **Protest crackdowns and media controls narrowed civilian opportunity** | **Amnesty International** | **2024-11-27** | [URL](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/11/urgent-and-transparent-investigation-needed-into-deadly-crackdown-on-opposition-protesters/) | Amnesty described deaths, mass detentions, and communications blackouts during the Islamabad crackdown. Even if not economic in the narrow sense, this worsened the environment ordinary people need for political voice and secure life chances. | `6B.10` | Other IDs: `6B.7`, `6B.8`, `6B.9`

**Search gap**
- I did not find direct 2024 household-panel or labor-market evidence showing that ordinary people’s incomes, job access, or mobility clearly improved year over year.
- Most usable evidence is indirect: macro stabilization, program design, and rights conditions.
- So the safest reading is: Sharif improved the macro setup and some delivery systems, but 2024 did not yet translate that into clearly better life chances for most ordinary people.
